subject: grid of scatterplots as mclust:clPairs using ggplot

messages.author: 4f6f5f995ee31178
messages.subject: grid of scatterplots as mclust:clPairs using ggplot
parts:
I have a data set such as:
https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/3180464/delme.rda

> load("delme.rda")
> print(delme[1:3,],digits=3)
WP km3int BBndvi2 SIPI PRI570 TO DCNI1
GR01WP01 GR01WP01 7 0.770 1.43 -0.0588 0.272 0.0396
GR01WP02 GR01WP02 6 0.781 1.41 -0.0594 0.266 0.0398
GR01WP03 GR01WP03 6 0.783 1.41 -0.0608 0.267 0.0404

and want to plot a matrix of scatter plots among variables
BBndvi2 SIPI PRI570 TO DCNI1
color-coding by the categorical variable km3int
in a similar way as done by mclust:clPairs()

I firts make the melted object:
SVISselm <- melt(delme,id.vars=c("WP","km3int"))
names(SVISselm)[3:4] <- c("Index","IndexValue")
SVISselm <- na.omit(SVISselm)
> SVISselm[1:3,]
WP km3int Index IndexValue
1 GR01WP01 7 BBndvi2 0.7703866
2 GR01WP02 6 BBndvi2 0.7810089
3 GR01WP03 6 BBndvi2 0.7826313

and then try:

ggplot() +
geom_point(data=SVISselm, mapping=aes(x=IndexValue, y=IndexValue,
color=km3int)) +
facet_grid(Index~Index)

but this is not at all what I wanted, as few scatterplots are actually
populated by dots.

Cannot figure out what I'm doing wrong, any help?

Thanks
Agus

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: grid of scatterplots as mclust:clPairs using ggplot
parts:
Hi:

I'd suggest looking at the ggpairs() function in the GGally package;
it is more general and behaves more closely to the pairs() function
from base graphics in terms of options than did the now deprecated
matrixplot() function in ggplot2.

Dennis

messages.author: dd68a26ecdacedb8
messages.subject: Re: grid of scatterplots as mclust:clPairs using ggplot
parts:
I second the reply to check out GGally.  Here is some code and output using GGally to maybe help out. A starting point to get more of what you want is to edit the upper = list(continuous = "density", combo = "box") argument.

Code snippet is below and link to gist is included at end of reply. The output from print(myPairs) looks useful to understanding the data set. This isn't validated and might only meet part of your requirements.

See link below to a .png of the plot output.

I took some liberties and removed missing values.

#install.packages("GGally")
require(GGally)
delme2 <- subset(delme[, c("km3int", "BBndvi2", "SIPI", "PRI570", "TO", "DCNI1")])
delme2 <- na.omit(delme2)
summary(delme2[1:10,])
head(delme2)
myPairs <- ggpairs(delme2[, 1:6],
    upper = list(continuous = "density", combo = "box"),
    lower = list(continuous = "points", combo = "dot"),
    color = "km3int",
    axisLabels = "show",
    title="Example Matrix for Exploration of delme Dataset")
print(myPairs)

Links to code and matrixplot output:

http://54.245.224.94/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2014/06/data-exploration-matrix-example-2.png

https://gist.github.com/sculpturearts/660b9b6c4b26283f8737

-Phil

messages.author: 4f6f5f995ee31178
messages.subject: Re: grid of scatterplots as mclust:clPairs using ggplot
parts:
Thanks to both of you
GGally definitely looks the way to go.
Nevertheless, I do have a problem with the legend,
and lacking a legend is the reason I am unhappy with clPairs().

Unfortunately, if I set legends=TRUE, I get a legend for
each plot, which is obviously inconvenient. I've seen
the discussion
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/22945702/how-to-add-an-external-legend-to-ggpairs

but it seems odd to me that such a general requirement (having one single legend
for one single color coding in all the graphics) implies such a
complex solution.
Is not there a simpler way of geting the single general color (and
eventually shape) legend as in ggplot?

Agus
